newsitem.title: FRANCE: Close that tunnel - France tells Israel.
newsitem.headline: Close that tunnel - France tells Israel.

text.p: France called on Israel on Thursday to close a disputed tunnel under the Arab Old City of Jersualem, the opening of which triggered the most serious Palestinian violence since the 1993 Israel-PLO peace accords.

"France asks all on the ground to keep their calm and reason, and to make the necessary calming gestures, in particular returning the tunnel under the Holy City to its initial state," a foreign ministry statement said.

Paris called for an immediate summit between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to resume peace negotiations and enable a full implementation of self-rule accords already signed.
It also asked the European Union to provide immediate special financial and humanitarian aid to help the Palestinian Authority cope with the crisis.
Earlier on Thursday, French President Jacques Chirac telephoned Arafat to express support and appeal for calm.
In a 20-minute phone call, Chirac "assured (Arafat) of his solidarity and support after the grave incidents in the Palestinian territories", the president's office said.

In an earlier statement, the Foreign Ministry accused Israel of triggering the violence, in which at least 44 Palestinians and 11 Israelis were killed, by opening the archeological tunnel close to al-Aqsa Mosque, one of Islam's holiest shrine.
It called the violence a worrying throwback to the 1987-93 Intifada, or uprising, against Israeli occupation.
A delegation of Arab ambassadors, including Palestinian envoy Leila Shahid, met the head of the French Foreign Ministry to thank France for its stance and ask it to continue.
